history.summary: CORRECTED CSV TOWN: the temple is at Hiyangthang (Hiyangthang village area, Wangoi), Imphal West district, on the hilltop of Heibok Ching about 10 km from Imphal city - not inside Imphal itself. IMPORTANT TRADITION NOTE: this is primarily a Sanamahism (traditional Meitei religion) temple, not a Hindu temple, though Hindu worship has co-existed here since the 18th century; keep-or-drop decision needed if the dataset is Hindu-temples-only. Legend tells that Irai Leima, daughter of Heibok Ningthou, fled the wrath of King Kwakpa of the Khuman dynasty and vanished beneath the granary floor of Sarangthem Luwangba, declaring herself his daughter and goddess. King Senbi Kiyamba (1467-1508) of the Ningthouja dynasty proclaimed her the goddess Hiyangthang Lairembi; the original shrine was created by Sarangthem Luwangba, and his family has held grand annual feasts (Chaklen Katpa) in her honour ever since. In the 18th century, during the reign of King Garib Niwaj (Pamheiba), the goddess was re-identified with the Hindu goddess Kamakhya (a form of Durga) and a Durga idol was installed beside Irai Leima, making this a rare site where Sanamahism and Hinduism blend. On 22 March 1979 an association was formed for the worship of Hiyangthang Lairembi (Ireima) in her traditional form. Thousands of devotees - largely women - gather at dawn on Bor Numit (the 3rd day of Durga Puja) for Bor Puja, believing the goddess grants wishes on that day.

name: Hiyangthang Lairembi Temple
town: Hiyangthang (CSV town 'Imphal' is incorrect - the temple is about 10 km from Imphal city)
town_description: Hiyangthang is a village area in Wangoi, Imphal West district, about 10 km from Imphal city. The temple crowns Heibok Ching (Heibok Hill), the sacred hill of the Irai Leima legend, in the rural Imphal valley fringe. It is one of Manipur's most important living sites of Meitei indigenous religion.
tradition: Sanamahism (Meitei religion), with Hindu syncretism since the 18th century
